messages.content: I need to retrieve server responses for certain user queries. Can you send a GET request to 'https://example.com/api/intent' for the following intents: ['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye']? Here are the user queries that need to be matched with the intents: ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds'].

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the server's response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent.

intents.description: A list of intent codes based on user queries, such as 'get_balance' and 'transfer_funds'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time in seconds to wait for the server response. The default is 2.5 seconds. This is a float type value.

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response, such as 'application/json'.

User-Agent.description: The user agent string of the software that is initiating the request, such as 'Mozilla/5.0'.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the GET request. If not provided, default headers will be used.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to send a GET request to 'https://example.com/api/intent' for the following intents: ['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye']. They also provide user queries: ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds'].

We need to interpret what they want. They say "retrieve server responses for certain user queries." They want us to send a GET request to the API endpoint for the intents. Possibly we need to pass the intents as query parameters or in the body? The function signature: get_response takes url, intents (list), timeout, headers. So we can call get_response with url='https://example.com/api/intent', intents=['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye'], maybe default timeout and headers.

But the user also gave user queries: ['hello', 'I want to transfer funds']. Maybe we need to match them with intents? But the function only accepts intents list. We could just pass the intents list. Or we might need to do something else: maybe we need to match each query to an intent and then call the API for each matched intent? But the function signature only allows one request per call. We could call it once with all intents. That seems fine.

Thus we should call the function get_response with url='https://example.com/api/intent', intents=['get_balance', 'transfer_funds', 'hello', 'goodbye'].

We should include the function call.
